verdict: All 17 acceptance criteria pass, and they pass under execution rather than by reading. node --check is clean; the export list is exactly the pinned thirteen; the globals grep returns only comment prose; there is no .from(/.rpc( anywhere else under public/src/transport; wallet_credit, Profile.gems, discord, webhook, FormData, createObjectURL and storage.from( are all zero; the only two throws are the documented persist() and ownCompanyId() chokepoints and neither escapes an export. I did not take the header's measurement block on trust: I rebuilt the driven harness against the SHIPPED file (the scratchpad copy it was originally run on is 99 lines older) and all 19 cases pass, including the two that matter most — a dispatch whose RPC refuses returns the cargo through the UNCAPPED refundRes path, and a settle answered retried:true credits nothing. I then wrote my own harness for the quote seam against routes.js's REAL meridianQuote() and confirmed all four claims independently: a bare quote answers quote_not_request having moved zero metal, the enriched object index.js actually sends reaches the RPC as exactly nine named arguments with p_units summed from the manifest (40) rather than read off the quote, dispatch({cargo:{}}) still answers bad_cargo, and an 80-unit manifest against a 40-unit fare is refused BEFORE the escrow runs while a 10-unit one ships. Against sql/038 on disk, every structural claim holds: transport_dispatch really does declare nine arguments, trg_ins really does pin runs_used/repairs_used/assigned_to/status, UPDATE really is revoked on both transport_companies and transport_rigs, and every column selected by myCompany/listMyRigs/listContracts exists. Money discipline is at or above cost.js: verify-then-deduct, unwind in reverse, refundRes for undo and addRes for payout with the distinction argued as a safety property, the repair bill routed through opEcon with an explicit refusal rather than an invented number, addGems carrying a named reason, and the delivered total MEASURED as a before/after delta instead of assumed from the request. Nothing here gates _convoyCanSend, nothing touches the Garage rail, and Meridian is treated as a ceiling in every message. What holds it back is not the code but the prose around it.
biggest_gap: dispatch() refunds the escrow on outcomes it cannot know, which can DUPLICATE the cargo. contracts.js:1087-1092 is `if (!r.ok) { held.refund(); return r; }` under the comment 'The RPC refused. The cargo never left, so put it back' — but !r.ok is not only a refusal. rpc() itself builds a `no_answer` envelope at :422-427 whose own fix line says 'the call may or may not have landed', and rpcFail() at :449 turns a thrown network error into the same !r.ok shape. If transport_dispatch actually committed and only the answer was lost, this line hands the manifest back to a shipper who is ALSO holding an in-transit contract carrying that same manifest — which transport_settle will deliver to them a second time. That is a cargo faucet sitting on exactly the refused-versus-unknown ambiguity the rest of the file is built to keep apart (the four-times bug, MISSING_RE's 'never used to decide the market is empty', the unknown-code arm that prints the code rather than guessing). The p_client_ref guard does not cover it: newRef() mints a fresh id on every call and index.js:1046 calls dispatch(q) with no clientRef on the quote, so no resend can ever match the ref and the idempotence sql/038 built is inert on the only live call path — which the file half-admits at :1103-1105 ('each attempt mints its own ref and therefore buys its own haul') while :1080-1083 still claims 'a resend of THIS call matches'. Fix is small and local: hold the escrow (do not refund) when the failure is unknown-outcome — r.code === 'no_answer', or a fail() with missing:false and no code — and say so in the envelope; and stamp a stable ref onto the route/quote object at the first attempt so a genuine resend is idempotent.
